content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with price overshoots, suggesting sentiment drives short-term volatility.", "Models exhibit mean-reversion bias in later cycles, underestimating sharp declines after peaks.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with historical price patterns, indicating sentiment calibration is critical.", "Early forecast lags often misalign with true price movements, especially during sharp reversals.", "Models show diminishing predictive power when sentiment is neutral or bearish, suggesting sentiment is a key signal.", "Forecast bias is strongest in the first 5 days of the 30-day window, indicating model calibration needs adjustment.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in forecasting when price volatility exceeds historical norms."]}
